page: Hetzner Cloud cpx62 is an x86_64 virtual server hosted on the QEMU hypervisor, utilizing AMD EPYC processors. This instance provides 16 shared vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 31.0 GB of system memory, which equates to approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 640 GB NVMe SSD, while dedicated GPU resources and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included. The processor architecture supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25 percent. Large-block memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read speeds reaching 277.56 GB/sec and write speeds at 137.51 GB/sec, both ranking in the top tier. Multi-threaded performance, such as bzip3 decompression, is strong, though overall multi-core CPU metrics from Passmark and Geekbench fall into the average tier. This discrepancy highlights a potential tradeoff where individual core performance is robust, but shared CPU allocation may limit sustained multi-core scaling under heavy concurrent loads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the cpx62 offers a high density of shared vCPUs and local NVMe storage relative to its resource class, making it a viable option for workloads that require moderate compute power without the premium cost of dedicated cores. It is well-suited for applications such as static web serving, text and image processing, lightweight database operations, and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks, where its strong single-thread performance and fast local storage can be fully leveraged.
